title: When a dedicated collector earns the handoff
decision: Choose between acquiring directly with the final tool and adding a separate floor collector.
analysis: 1746’s inclined lift and shared wristed hand keep the piece in the same tool from acquisition to placement. 1325 shows a separate way to simplify a shared tool. Its dossier describes fixing the grip spacing while retaining the articulated arm. 6328’s released code exposes both a direct floor sweep and a dedicated cube handoff, so its added collector can be evaluated as an optional path rather than a universal requirement.
check: Time approach, acquisition, transfer, scoring and recovery together. Test off-angle pieces and interruptions at the collector-to-hand boundary. A dedicated collector earns its space when its wider capture envelope more than offsets the added transfer and service burden.

title: Where to put the work of turning
decision: Decide whether to rotate the whole chassis, route the piece through the robot, or rotate the scoring assembly.
analysis: Lockdown and Lemon Zest illustrate front-and-back delivery with a wristed tool on an elevator during POWER UP. Backlash solved a different access problem with a rotating scoring assembly in DEEP SPACE. Compare which turn the mechanism avoids, where it moves the occupied envelope and what it does to wiring and alignment. The ability to rotate or release on two sides only saves a cycle if the field route lets the robot use it.
check: Draw pickup and target headings on the field first. Trace the loaded mechanism and bumper envelope through each transition. Compare the travel time saved with the added deployment, repeatability and repair costs under the same driving assumptions.

title: A wide shooter needs a route that can keep it fed
decision: Choose a fuel path and scoring route as one system.
analysis: 125 packages a circular serializer around a center-fed turret to gain aiming freedom. 2481 uses a wide fixed discharge path and accepts a loaded bump crossing. 7769 removed a divider that constrained real feed and linked its mechanism layout to service and defense problems. 2910’s original and rebuilt versions illustrate why a robot’s acquisition and release paths must be read together before borrowing a named mechanism.
check: Measure acquired, retained and scored fuel over an entire active window. Run with a full hopper and near-empty hopper, partial battery, route interference and a feed jam. Compare the complete rate and recovery time instead of comparing bench burst speeds.

title: When the climber sets the layout
decision: Test whether an endgame mechanism justifies the space and load path it requires.
analysis: 1619’s central climbing layout shaped where its cargo elevator and shooter could fit. 604’s released climb logic shows how reaches, partial lifts and handoffs must be distinct recoverable states. In 2026, 7769’s prototype notes show the opposite pressure when a proposed endgame device competes with scoring hardware for space. Compare endgame value under each game’s actual scoring rules and time window.
check: Lay out the worst-case loaded climb and normal scoring states before selecting actuator locations. Track route time and service conflicts, then compare the expected match contribution with the cost of keeping the secondary mechanism.
